description: Soil and Water Conservation explores the ground beneath us and the water that moves through it: how soil forms, erosion and how to control it, watersheds and aquifers, the water cycle, water pollution and treatment, and hands-on conservation work.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Soil
requirements.summary: What soil is, how it forms and the main plant nutrients.

requirements.title: Erosion
requirements.summary: What erosion is, its effects and its types, with examples.

requirements.title: Conservation practices
requirements.summary: What conservation means and how erosion-control methods work.

requirements.title: Watersheds
requirements.summary: Watersheds, river basins and aquifers, and mapping a watershed.

requirements.title: The water cycle
requirements.summary: The hydrologic cycle, how soil holds water, and how land use affects water supply.

requirements.title: Water pollution
requirements.summary: Sources and effects of water pollution and how wastewater is treated.

requirements.title: Conservation field work
requirements.summary: Two options, such as a site visit, planting trees, seeding an area or tackling a local erosion or pollution problem.
